data.name: Mandos

engine.because: Needs our engine fork's build until a Neo Angband release carries our pull requests: neo-angband PR #429 (the door-close loop, #428), PR #432 (input-flush, #414) and PR #433 (the master seed, #431), on diegoami/neo-angband's neowarrior-lab branch, whose engine reports 1.23.0-beta.2-mandos.N. Also the first line with mod API 2, the truth domain and the loadout simulation.

data.description:
Mandos, formerly better-borg: a class-agnostic Borg - a hard fork of Angband's automatic player (the borg in Angband 4.2.6, as ported to Neo Angband by neostryder) carrying defect fixes and strength improvements for every class. You choose the classes and races it may play: one toggle per class and per race, and each new character is drawn from the ones switched on (all of them by default). A warrior is born through the archived neowarrior-borg fork's measured plan; every other class through the game's own suggested stats. It grinds for you: it plays unattended, concentrates on reaching a chosen stage reliably, retires each successful run into a kept, loadable save, and starts the next character when one dies. Deterministic, plays by the same rules as the stock Borg. Port defects are staged here as upstream pull requests; improvements upstream declines still live here.

Installing and enabling it does not give it your character. Start it from the title screen's New Mandos character row, or press Ctrl-Z in play to hand over the keyboard, as with the stock Borg.
data.author: diegoami

rules.title: Play risky
rules.description: borg_plays_risky. Skip the early hit-point and character-level gates that hold the Borg above a depth, wait longer before drinking a cure, and back away later in a losing fight. It reaches deeper sooner and dies more.

rules.title: Value melee and missile damage
rules.description: borg_worships_damage. Add weight to weapon and bow damage when the Borg scores a set of gear, so a trade that costs armour for damage looks better than it otherwise would.

rules.title: Value speed
rules.description: borg_worships_speed. Add weight to a speed bonus when scoring gear.

rules.title: Value hit points
rules.description: borg_worships_hp. Add weight to constitution and hit points when scoring gear.

rules.title: Value spell points
rules.description: borg_worships_mana. Add weight to spell points when scoring gear. Has no effect on a warrior, who has no spell points.

rules.title: Value armour class
rules.description: borg_worships_ac. Add weight to armour class when scoring gear.

rules.title: Value gold
rules.description: borg_worships_gold. Sell harder, walk down rather than pay for a recall, and put off the first deep recall. It buys better equipment sooner and spends longer in town doing it. Upstream stops applying this past character level 20.

rules.title: Save up for something it wants
rules.description: borg_self_scum. Let the Borg set itself a gold target and work in town until it can afford one item it has decided it needs. It only does this from character level 10, with a permanent light source and food in the pack.

rules.title: Skimp on stockpiles for an early munchkin run
rules.description: borg_munchkin_start. Below character level borg_munchkin_level (12), value stockpiles of resist poison and speed potions, phase door, word of recall and the deeper cures less than it normally would, on the assumption that a young character is cashing out early. Upstream, this setting also makes the Borg stair-scum for loot to sell at this stage. That part is not ported, so here it changes what the Borg carries and leaves how it dives alone.

settings.title: Stage character level
settings.description: The character level a run must reach for the Borg to count it as having attained its target stage, together with borg.stageDepth. A run that attains is saved under a library name and the next character starts. The default (2) is the stage baseline's calibration (2026-11-03): the strongest rung today's Borg attains on half the standard seed grid; raise it as the Borg grows stronger. Read once per page, so a change applies to the next birth.

settings.title: Stage depth
settings.description: The dungeon depth a run must have arrived on (0 is the town) for the Borg to count it as having attained its target stage, together with borg.stageClvl. The default (1) is the stage baseline's calibration (2026-11-03); the owner's destination is a moderate depth at character level around 20, which the settings reach as the Borg grows stronger. Read once per page, so a change applies to the next birth.

settings.title: Death replay release turn
settings.description: The death-replay trainer's release point (#29): when the game's turn counter reaches this value the Borg stops playing and hands the keyboard back with the death banner, so the owner can play the last turns of a dead run themselves. Take the number from the dossier ladder's release-boundary line (docs/runs/, the run's postmortem directory); 0 (the default) keeps the replay mode off. Birth the character on the recorded seed (?seed=<S>&new, the dossier names the race settings) - the Borg replays the run deterministically to this turn. Read once per page, so the release point is fixed for the whole life.

settings.title: Death replay death turn
settings.description: The recorded death turn the death-replay banner counts down from (#29): with borg.replayReleaseTurn armed, the banner names this turn and how many turns remain. Take it from the dossier's recorded-death line; 0 (the default) shows the banner without the countdown. Read once per page with borg.replayReleaseTurn.
